name: execline
why: A scripting language with no interpreter that chains programs directly, a strange and rewarding way to think about shells.

brief.what_it_is: execline is a non-interactive scripting language from skarnet.org, described as being like sh but with a quite different syntax. Its execlineb program is meant to be used as an interpreter for a text file, so a script is run by handing the file to execlineb. The other commands (cd, if, forx, elglob, and so on) are meant to be used inside an execlineb script. The homepage says it has conditional loops, getopt-style option handling and filename globbing. The homepage does not describe the inputs and outputs in detail beyond running scripts.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage's stated motivation is that execline is as powerful as a shell but its syntax is more logical and predictable than the shell's, and it has no security issues. A separate page, 'Why not just use /bin/sh?', is linked from the homepage but I did not fetch it.
brief.how_it_works: Scripts are run through the execlineb program used as an interpreter. Each command in a script chains directly into the next program rather than being evaluated by an interpreter loop, so the script effectively execs programs in sequence. The homepage does not spell out the mechanism further, and the design-and-grammar page was not followed.

commands_seen.context: Named on the homepage as the script parser and launcher, used as the interpreter for a text file. No literal invocation line appeared on the homepage.
Repository checkout command given on the Download section for the execline git repository.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists requirements: a POSIX-compliant system with a standard C development environment, and GNU make 3.81 or later. skalibs 2.16.0.0 or later is a build-time requirement, and also a run-time requirement if linking against the shared skalibs library. Optional: if using musl and wanting nsswitch-like functionality, nsss 0.2.1.3 or later is needed at build time and boot time. Compilation is described in an INSTALL file that ships with the source. Starting with 2.9.2.0 there is a --enable-multicall configure option to save disk space. The homepage does not mention Homebrew or any first-run configuration.
brief.standout: The language has no interpreter loop; the script is a chain of programs connected directly, and the whole package is a set of small single-purpose commands. The page also includes a set of quines, including one by Sertonix that uses only execline-package commands and no external programs.
brief.status: Appears maintained: the homepage names current release 2.10.0.0 and points to git mirrors on Codeberg, GitHub and SourceHut. I could not find a release date or last-commit date on the homepage, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: Non-interactive only; it is not a login or interactive shell (the homepage's own words are that the commands are 'essentially useful inside an execlineb script'). Requires skalibs as a build-time dependency, and as a run-time dependency when linked against the shared library. The optional nsss dependency is only for musl users wanting nsswitch-like behaviour. The homepage lists no Homebrew packaging notes; the brew_caveats field was empty. The execline_quines and exit-code conventions are documented on the homepage, but I did not check them beyond what the page states.
quotes: execline is a (non-interactive) scripting language, like sh - but its syntax is quite different from a traditional shell syntax.
Meanwhile, its syntax is far more logical and predictable than the shell's syntax, and has no security issues.
execline is free software. It is available under the ISC license.
fetch_log: https://skarnet.org/software/execline/ — fetched OK; returned the homepage text including requirements, licence, download and command reference list. No README fetch was needed or made. Other pages linked from it (design and grammar, 'Why not just use /bin/sh?', man pages) were not fetched because their exact URLs were not given in the page text.
